slides.title: Requirement and design
keyPoints: Chapter 13’s original offset example uses deliberately small values.
A reusable integer batch update needs a stronger rule: either every element can accept the offset, or no element.
The companion’s checked_offset program implements that rule with two passes.
The first pass validates; only a completely successful validation permits the second pass to mutate.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 22, use Requirement and design as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Chapter 13’s original offset example uses deliberately small values. A reusable integer batch update needs a stronger rule: either every element can accept the offset, or no element is changed. The companion’s checked_offset program implements that rule with two passes. The first pass validates; only a completely successful validation permits the second pass to mutate. Checking for overflow by performing the overflowing addition first would defeat the purpose. Instead, the code compares the existing value with a safe bound derived from the offset. For a positive offset, the largest permitted starting value is maximum - offset. For a negative offset, the smallest permitted starting value is minimum - offset. The sign guards make those bound calculations representable for the relevant cases. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. Have learners connect the words on the slide to an observable artifact before moving on.

slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 22, use Trace the evidence as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. The valid fixture changes one, two, and three into three, four, and five. The overflow fixture places a maximum integer after an ordinary first value, then requests an offset of one. This ordering matters: a one-pass implementation that updates as it checks might change the first value before discovering the impossible last value. Comparing the entire vector with its saved copy exposes that partial update. The underflow case checks the opposite boundary. Extreme offsets and an empty vector exercise additional paths without assuming a fixed width for int. The implementation uses numeric limits from the actual selected type, keeping the argument about representability connected to that type rather than a handwritten machine-specific constant. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 22, use Run and extend as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Build the checked_offset target and run its CTest fixture. Then add a mixed positive/negative vector and offsets of zero, one, and negative one. For every rejected case, compare the complete prior collection rather than only its size. Equal size does not prove equal contents. The two-pass solution is intentionally straightforward. A transactional update could also create a transformed copy and replace the original only after success, trading additional storage and copying for another implementation shape. Both approaches need a clear failure contract. Choose based on the type’s operations and workload rather than assuming that one generic pattern fits every collection. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. checks.prompt: Why is empty stderr worth saying out loud?
checks.answer: Because it proves normal results are not being smuggled through the diagnostic channel; many automated tests and scripts distinguish stdout from stderr.

checks.prompt: How should you explain exit code 0?
checks.answer: It is the process-level success signal. It does not replace checking stdout; it only says the program finished without reporting process failure.

slides.title: Transfer units as one transaction
keyPoints: Initial counts are 0 through 1000. Reject bad indices, negative amount, insufficient source, or a destination above 1000. A same-index transfer succeeds without change when the amount is available. Any rejection leaves stock unchanged.
slides.narration: Complete prevalidation works because the subsequent bounded int updates cannot fail. Same-object aliasing is handled before the two writes. A successful distinct-index transfer preserves total units. Rejection and same-index success preserve all counts. Alternative: A candidate copy works for more complex transactions, but these two bounded, nonthrowing writes need only a complete precheck.
